target_customer: Individuals and small organizations wanting to build wiki-style websites with custom design templates
problem: Wikis were hard to style and use as flexible websites; Infogami offered a wiki platform with designable pages.
business_model: hosted wiki platform, revenue model not stated by sources found

founders.name: Aaron Swartz
education: Stanford, dropped out to continue Infogami (per Wikipedia summary)
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page. He created web.py while building Infogami.

founders.name: Simon Carstensen
founders.background_notes: Named as a founder by a blog post on the first YC batch, not by the YC page.

exit.reason: Infogami could not find further funding, and YC organizers suggested merging with Reddit.

competitors.name: JotSpot
competitors.what: Wiki application platform with application templates

technical_complexity.rationale: A hosted wiki platform with templating needed a custom web framework, which Swartz built as web.py.

defensibility.rationale: Wiki platforms were numerous and a hosted wiki with no network effect was easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: JotSpot was bought by Google in 2006. Infogami itself merged into Reddit's parent in Nov 2005 and the platform was later used for Open Library.

market_need_then: eWeek reported in March 2005 that wiki vendors such as JotSpot and Socialtext were drawing customers and funding, showing demand for hosted wikis.

branding.domain_note: infogami.com now shows an unrelated London business intelligence firm per the YC page text; original domain history not found.
branding.community_and_virality: Software later powered Open Library, per Open Library developer docs.

brand_strength.rationale: No sources show the Infogami brand drawing users; fame came from its founder and later Reddit.

outcome_analysis: Infogami was a wiki platform started by Aaron Swartz in YC Summer 2005. After the summer it failed to raise further funding, and YC organizers pushed a merger with fellow batch company Reddit in November 2005, creating Not A Bug, which Conde Nast bought in October 2006. The wiki product was dropped as a business but its software was later reused for Open Library. Competition from funded wiki platforms such as JotSpot is plausible context, not a stated cause.
notes: The YC page description and the infogami.com content describe an unrelated London business intelligence firm, so the dataset one_liner is not about this company. infogami.com returned HTTP 503. Founders: the blog lists Carstensen, the YC page lists Swartz only. Sources differ on merger vs acquisition (Graham says merger; Ohanian says acquisition). No funding amounts found; seedtable lists none.
